'''Ekaterina Andreyevna Salnikova''' ({{Langx|ru|Екатерина Андреевна Сальникова}}; 8 December 1928 – 3 October 2016) was a Russian chemist working at the Berezniki Nitrogen and Fertilizer Plant. She was a gas welder's apprentice, a operator in the contact section, foreman in the catalyst mesh restoration department and then as a catalysis engineer and process engineer before retiring in 1976. Salnikova was a member of the [[Central Auditing Commission of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] and a [[Central Committee of the 24th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union|candidate member]] of the [[Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]]. She was awarded the [[Medal "For Distinguished Labour"]]; the [[Medal "For Labour Valour"]]; the [[Order of the Badge of Honour]]; the [[Jubilee Medal "In Commemoration of the 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin"]]; the [[Order of Lenin]] and the title of [[Hero of Socialist Labour]].

== Biography ==
Salnikova was born in the village of Shevaldino, now [[Usolsky District, Perm Krai|Usolsky District]], [[Perm Krai]] on 8 December 1928.<ref name="HeroesEntry">{{cite web |last=Karimov |first=Timur |title=Сальникова Екатерина Андреевна |trans-title=Salnikova Ekaterina Andreevna |URL=https://warheroes.ru/hero/hero.asp?Hero_id=26680 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=Heroes of the Country |language=ru}}</ref><ref name="CPSUBio">{{cite book |last=Goryachev |first=Yuri Vasilyevich |url=https://archive.org/details/2015_20220814/ |title=Центральный Комитет КПСС, ВКП(б), РКП(б), РСДРП(б). Историко Биографический Справочник |publisher=Granitsa |year=2015 |location=Moscow, Russia |pages=808–809 |language=ru |trans-title=Central Committee of the CPSU, All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks), Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks), Russian Social Democratic Labor Party (Bolsheviks). Historical and Biographical Reference Guide |chapter=Сальникова Екатерина Андреевна |trans-chapter=Salnikova Ekaterina Andreevna |url-access=registration |via=[[Internet Archive]]}}</ref> In 1943, during the [[Great Patriotic War (term)|Great Patriotic War]], she started her career as a gas welder's apprentice at the Berezniki Nitrogen and Fertilizer Plant, [[Berezniki]] before becoming a heat-exchange boiler stoker. As she continued working, Salinkova While finished high school, vocational school, and a two-year course at a master's school.<ref name="HeroesEntry" /><ref name="SolidarityArticle">{{cite news |last=Ryzhenkova |first=Yulia |date=9 April 2025 |title=Химия стратегического назначения |trans-title=Strategic Chemistry |url=https://www.solidarnost.org/articles/himiya-strategicheskogo-naznacheniya.html |access-date=30 August 2026 |work=Solidarity |language=ru}}</ref> She did welding on automobiles and operated heat-exchange machines.<ref name="CPSUBio" /><ref name="GSE1966Entry">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/ezhegodnik_bse_1966 |title=Great Soviet Encyclopedia Yearbook of 1966 |date=4 August 1996 |publisher=Sovetskaya Entsiklopediya |editor-last=Shaumyan |editor-first=Lev |editor-link=Lev Shaumyan |edition=10th |location=Moscow, Russia |page=610 |chapter=Сальникова Екатерина Андреевна |trans-chapter=Salnikova Ekaterina Andreevna |url-access=registration |via=[[Internet Archive]]}}</ref> From August 1950, Salinikova worked as an operator in the contact section of the Berezniki Nitrogen and Fertilizer Plant.<ref name="GSE1966Entry" />

Between 1968 and 1976, she was a senior worker at the Berezniki Nitrogen and Fertiliser Plant (foreman in the catalyst mesh restoration department and then as a catalysis engineer and process engineer) before retiring in 1976.<ref name="CPSUBio" /><ref name="SolidarityArticle" /> Salnikova was a participant in the introduction of new types of catalysts into production and the development of new units, the inclusion of which in the production process enabled the plant to significantly reduce the costs of producing the product. Her team successfully implemented several of their own ideas, seeing significant economic benefits.<ref name="HeroesEntry" />

She became a member of the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] in 1957.<ref name="CPSUBio" /><ref name="GSE1966Entry" /> Salinikova was appointed a member of the [[Central Auditing Commission of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] by the [[23rd Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] and was in the role between 1966 and 1971.<ref name="HeroesEntry" /><ref name="GSE1966Entry" /> She was a delegate to both the 23rd Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1966 and [[24th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] in 1971.<ref name="HeroesEntry" /><ref name="SolidarityArticle" /> Salinikova was a [[Central Committee of the 24th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union|candidate member]] of the [[Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] from 1971 to 1976.<ref name="CPSUBio" /> Further, she was an elected member of the {{Interlanguage link|Perm Regional Committee|ru|Пермский областной комитет КПСС}} and the Berezniki City Committee of the CPSU.<ref name="HeroesEntry" />

== Personal life ==
Salnikova was married to Yakov Aleksandrovich Salnikov for 50 years.<ref name="SolidarityArticle" /> She was resident in Berezniki and died on 3 October 2016.<ref name="HeroesEntry" />

== Recognition ==
On 5 January 1950, Salnikova was a recipient of the [[Medal "For Distinguished Labour"]]; the [[Medal "For Labour Valour"]] on 5 November 1954; and the [[Order of the Badge of Honour]] on 28 May 1966;<ref name="HeroesEntry" /> and the [[Jubilee Medal "In Commemoration of the 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin"]] in 1970.<ref name="SolidarityArticle" /> She was conferred the title of [[Hero of Socialist Labour]], the [[Order of Lenin]] and the Hammer and Sickle gold medal by the [[Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union]] on 15 January 1974.<ref name="HeroesEntry" /> Salnikova was made an honorary citizen of the city of Berezniki in 1987.<ref name="SolidarityArticle" />
